newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas down after analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: Adidas down after analyst meeting.

text.p: Shares in German sportswear group Adidas AG slumped about four percent in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings following a meeting with analysts.

Adidas shares were down 6.20 marks at 162.30 marks and off the high for the day at 173 marks reached after Adidas said earlier on Tuesday that operating profit in 1996 nearly doubled to 360 marks as sales surged 35 percent to 4.71 billion marks ($2.8 billion).
One analyst, who asked not to be identified, said the drop was likely tied to profit-taking after recent strong gains in Adidas shares and that the meeting was overall positive.

"It was a good meeting and Adidas was upbeat," the analyst said. "The company said sales would keep growing along with profits but that promotional expenses would also rise, which was negative but not overwhelming."
Another analyst also said the meeting was overall positive and said the drop in Adidas was due to profit-taking.

Adidas earlier on Tuesday held a news conference at which it said the 1996 dividend payout would be raised to 1.10 marks per share from 25 pfennigs in 1995 and that double-digit profit growth was expected to continue in the coming years.
